summary: This bill increases the maximum federal share of funding for certain water infrastructure projects to 90% of the total project cost, prioritizing projects in severe drought areas, low-income communities, or those deemed regionally or nationally significant for water supply, reuse, or environmental benefits.

scores.thoughts: This bill increases the maximum federal assistance for certain water infrastructure projects from 49% to 90% of the total project cost, and prioritizes financing for these projects. This directly leads to more federal spending on these projects.

The bill aims to provide increased federal assistance for water infrastructure projects in areas experiencing severe drought, and for projects that increase drinking water supply, enhance water reuse/recycling, or provide environmental benefits. This directly supports efforts to mitigate the effects of drought and improve water management, which are environmental protection measures.

The bill raises the federal cost-share cap to 90% for qualifying drought-related water infrastructure projects and directs the Secretary/Administrator to prioritize financing for them. This directly increases potential federal outlays without any offsetting revenue or cuts, pushing the bill toward accepting larger deficits to fund priorities.
